lessons.title: have/has in the Simple Present
lessons.content: The verb 'have' is used as a main verb to show ownership or possession. In Simple Present, use 'have' with I, we, you, and they. Use 'has' with he, she, and it.

details.subject: I / We / You / They
details.burmese: ကျွန်မ ကားတစ်စီး ရှိတယ်။

details.subject: He / She / It
details.burmese: သူမ ဘေလွင့်တံ အများကြီး ရှိတယ်။

lessons.title: had in the Simple Past
lessons.content: In Simple Past, we use 'had' for all subjects. 'Had' is the past form of 'have'. Use time markers like 'before', 'yesterday', 'last week', 'two days ago' with Simple Past.

details.subject: All subjects
details.burmese: အရင်က ကျွန်မ ကားတစ်စီး ရှိခဲ့တယ်။

details.subject: All subjects (negative)
details.example: I didn't have a car before.
details.burmese: အရင်က ကျွန်မ ကားတစ်စီး မရှိခဲ့ဘူး။

details.subject: All subjects (question)
details.example: Did I have a car before?
details.burmese: အရင်က ကျွန်မ ကားတစ်စီး ရှိခဲ့လား။

lessons.title: Perfect Tenses with have
lessons.content: The verb 'have' is used as an auxiliary verb in the perfect tenses. Present Perfect uses have/has + V3, Past Perfect uses had + V3, and Future Perfect uses will have + V3.

examples: I have walked on this path before.
He has written several movie scripts.
She has been here for twenty minutes.
We had met him before he became famous.
She had established her company before 2008.
I will have left for my trip.
We will have finished our project.
You will have sent the document by Tuesday.

lessons.title: Sentence Forms with have
lessons.content: When making negative and interrogative sentences with 'have' as a main verb, we use 'do/does/did' as an auxiliary verb. 'Do not have' / 'Does not have' / 'Did not have' for negatives, and 'Do/Does/Did + subject + have' for questions.

lessons.title: Short Answers with have
lessons.content: When replying to Yes/No questions about 'have', use short answers with the same auxiliary verb used in the question.

details.question: Did you have a car before?
Will you have a car next year?
Has she been here for twenty minutes?
Had he met her before the party?
Will they have finished by tomorrow?
